subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for FinPay (predictable TPS & isolation)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — Dedicated capacity fit (FinPay)

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points / goals
- Production tail-latency spikes impacting end-user experience (sporadic 99th percentile latency > 500ms).
- Cost variability on current public-hosted endpoints, especially during peak batch jobs.
- Need for data isolation for payments data (compliance + internal policy).
- Want predictable throughput for peak traffic around batch settlement windows.

What we learned about your current stack
- Using a managed hosted API for model inference (third-party provider) for customer-facing generation.
- Models: primarily a fine-tuned open LLM (approx 1.3B–3B parameter family) with seq lengths up to ~1024 tokens.
- Traffic: baseline ~40 TPS, predictable peak ~200 TPS for 15–30 minute windows, occasional bursts to ~350–400 TPS for <10 minutes during heavy settlement windows.
- Batching is handled client-side; they currently run a homegrown queue + autoscaling on VMs for worker processes.
- Concerned about KV-cache warmup and burst cold-starts increasing latency.

Success criteria for a Dedicated capacity fit
- Sustained 200 TPS with 99th percentile latency < 150ms for typical prompts (seq_len ~512).
- Ability to absorb bursts to 400 TPS within a 5-minute ramp window without SLA violations.
- Data isolation (single-tenant GPU pools, SOC2 evidence for controls).
- Predictable per-token and per-hour costs for budget planning.

Initial sizing and technical notes (high level)
- Based on your current model family and sequence lengths we estimated a Dedicated pool of 8–12 A100-class GPUs (or equivalent) with autoscaling headroom for burst capacity. Exact sizing requires a short perf test.
- Key infra requirements: private VPC networking, strict egress rules, and customer-managed KMS for keys (you flagged KMS requirement).

Open questions / clarifications
- Can you share typical request size distribution (percentile of short vs long prompts)?
- Any hard requirements for retention/audit log window beyond standard SOC2 (e.g., 12 months)?
- Who owns procurement/contract reviews on your side (legal or ops)?

Next steps
1) Rishi to run a short technical deep-dive to validate perf assumptions and confirm GPU class + exact node count (can we schedule 60 mins next week?).
2) I’ll share a Dedicated capacity overview + a mutual action plan (attached).
3) If perf checks out, we’ll propose a 30-day trial with reserved capacity + defined burst policy.
4) Procurement: exchange initial SOW/term sheet and DocuSign link for review.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-capacity-overview.pdf (PDF), finpay_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (Excel)

Thanks again — I’ve put proposed times for the technical deep-dive below. If any of the above is off, please reply inline.

Proposed deep-dive slots (PT): Tue 3/16 10:00–11:00, Wed 3/17 15:00–16:00, Thu 3/18 08:30–09:30

—

Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Dedicated capacity fit (FinPay)

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap, this looks right to me. Quick answers inline:

- Request size distribution: ~70% short prompts (<128 tokens), ~25% mid (128–512), ~5% long (>512).
- Retention: Compliance requires 18 months for audit logs (we have SOC2, and some payment records need 18 months).
- Procurement: Legal handles contract redlines, but Ops owns the implementation timeline. I’ll loop in Legal once we have an SOW.

We’re very sensitive to tail-latency — anything that reduces cold-starts and preserves KV-cache across requests would be valuable. The burst numbers match what we see in production logs.

I’ll take Tue 3/16 10:00 if that works for Rishi. Also please send the mutual action plan — I want to share it with Ops before the deep-dive.

—Alex

Adding some technical context ahead of our deep-dive:

- We’ll validate throughput by running 2 perf tests: 1) steady-state 200 TPS with representative prompt mix, 2) burst ramp 50→400 TPS over 5 minutes to observe cold-start behavior and cache warm-up.
- Typical optimizations we’ll test: server-side continuous batching, KV-cache pre-warming, and quantization profile that matches your model family to reduce memory footprint.
- For isolation we’ll recommend a single-tenant pool with private subnet + customer KMS. We can show SOC2 evidence in the console and provide exportable audit logs.
- For autoscaling/burst: we support configurable burst pools (reserved baseline + burst nodes for short windows). We’ll instrument an SLO test to measure 99th percentile latency under the burst policy.

Requested items before the deep-dive:
1) Sample request/response logs (anonymized) showing latency distribution (helpful but not mandatory).
2) A brief description of any pre- or post-processing you run that could affect latency (e.g., long tokenization steps or third-party enrichment).

I can take Tue 3/16 10:00 PT. I’ll prepare a short test plan and an initial sizing recommendation to share during the call.

—Rishi
